subject: Deployment model qualification & security evidence — CareHaven
messages:

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap & next steps from today's call — CareHaven deployment model

Hi Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap and clear next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

Call highlights
- Primary requirement: CareHaven needs an inference deployment that meets HIPAA controls and can sign a BAA.
- Traffic profile: bursty inference workload (peaks ~120 rps, sustained ~15 rps), low latency for real-time triage.
- Data residency: US-only; logs retained for 90 days for audit but customer data must be segregated.

Deployment options discussed (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, but needs clarification on BAA scope and customer data residency controls.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput; can be isolated per-tenant and restrict egress, easier for contract-level BAA carve-outs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, preferred by InfoSec for PHI in some customers, longer lead time and ops overhead.

Action items (owners + ETA)
1) CareHaven: send back the filled security questionnaire and list of required audit artifacts (Priya) — ETA Wed 10/21 EOD.
2) Redwood: provide SOC 2 scope doc, BAA draft, and a short one-page mapping that shows which deployment modes meet each CareHaven control (Jasmine + Karthik) — ETA Thu 10/22.
3) Redwood: cost sketch for Dedicated vs Private including expected provisioning lead time (Marissa) — ETA Fri 10/23.

Attachments referenced: CareHaven_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (you mentioned you'll return this)

If the timeline above works, we'll prepare the BAA draft and a short SOC2 evidence bundle for your security team to review.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Jasmine — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming a few points from our end: 

1) We'll return the completed security questionnaire by EOD tomorrow (10/21).
2) Our InfoSec has a hard requirement that any hosted service must be covered by a signed BAA and demonstrate customer data separation + ability to disable telemetry/log-sharing on a per-tenant basis.
3) If Redwood can show a Dedicated option where the instance is single-tenant with network ACLs and optional private peering, that's our preference for the pilot. Private/on-prem is still on the table if the Dedicated option requires more changes than expected.

One additional ask: can you outline what items in your SOC 2 report map to the HIPAA controls we listed (specifically access controls, encryption in transit and at rest, and change management)? Our security team would like this in writing for the intake.

Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps from today's call — CareHaven deployment model

Priya — thanks for the questionnaire, skimmed it and pulled out the quick mapping here to speed things up. I'll follow with the cost sketch later today.

Short mapping to the three deployment modes (operational tradeoffs):
- Hosted API
  - Pros: fastest time-to-prod, managed upgrades, shorter legal cycle if BAA covers hosted.
  - Cons: multi-tenant runtime unless Dedicated is selected; telemetry/analytics pipeline is centralized by default but we can disable per-tenant telemetry and provide log export.
  - HIPAA considerations: can meet encryption in transit/rest and IAM controls; InfoSec will want evidence (SOC 2 + config guide + access logs).

- Dedicated capacity (recommended for pilot)
  - Pros: single-tenant GPU pool, VPC peering option, dedicated storage for KV cache, separate service account and IAM boundaries. Predictable throughput for your burst profile.
  - Cons: provisioning lead (typically 2-4 weeks depending on region), higher monthly commit.
  - HIPAA considerations: enableable to satisfy BAA requirements for PHI processing, easier to show separation during an audit.

- Private VPC / On-prem
  - Pros: maximum isolation, you control the network and audit logs.
  - Cons: longer procurement and ops, potential versioning lag, and on-prem will require our deployment engineers to run an install window.

Requested deliverables from Redwood today: 
1) Short mapping doc (we'll send as part of the SOC2 bundle).
2) BAA draft to start legal review — attached is a redline template we usually send first.
3) Cost sketch for Dedicated vs Private (will send by EOD).

Hope this helps — will include concrete numbers in the cost sketched doc.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps from today's call — CareHaven deployment model

Marissa — thanks, that mapping is useful. A couple follow-ups from our security team after reviewing your initial notes: 

- Can you confirm whether Dedicated capacity still routes through Redwood-managed telemetry collectors (i.e., will logs ever traverse a multi-tenant analytics pipeline)? If so, we need a design note on how telemetry can be excluded or restricted.
- For the BAA: we want to start with a draft and have Redwood confirm whether Dedicated qualifies under your standard BAA or whether we need an expanded scope.
- For SOC2 evidence: our auditor has flagged two things they will want to see for the intake — (1) evidence of key rotation policy and (2) a sample access log showing token usage tied to a tenant-id. Can you provide these as examples rather than full production logs?

If you can provide a short one-page technical note on telemetry/data-flow for Dedicated (where logs live, where they can be exported, retention controls) and the SOC2 artifacts mentioned, we can get the intake moving quickly.

We'll plan a follow-up call next week to walk through the SOC2 bundle and contract timeline.

Best,
Priya

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps from today's call — CareHaven deployment model

Hi Priya — following up with the short artifacts you requested. See bullets below and attached stubs.

1) Telemetry/data-flow note for Dedicated: 
- Dedicated runs in a single-tenant GPU pool. By default, telemetry (service metrics and anonymized usage telemetry) is collected by Redwood's monitoring plane, but per-tenant telemetry ingestion can be disabled. Logs (request/response traces) for Dedicated are stored in an isolated S3 bucket per-customer and are not merged into multi-tenant analytics unless explicitly opted in. We can provide a VPC peering option so your team can pull logs directly into your SIEM.

2) SOC2 artifacts (sample stubs attached): 
- key-rotation-policy.pdf (sample redwood policy describing automatic rotation schedule and manual rotation for emergency key compromise)
- access-log-sample.txt (redacted token usage showing tenant-id binding; timestamps and request-ids preserved; all PHI redacted)

3) BAA scope: Dedicated is covered under Redwood's standard BAA if the customer has a dedicated environment and signs the BAA. Private/on-prem will require a slightly different exhibit but we can start with the standard BAA draft attached and iterate.

Attachments included: key-rotation-policy.pdf (PDF, 18 KB); access-log-sample.txt (TXT, 6 KB); BAA-draft-carehaven.docx (DOCX, 48 KB)

Next steps: Jasmine will schedule a technical deep-dive next week (your availability?) and Marissa will share the Dedicated vs Private cost sketch.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
